title: Strict semilinear scalar comparison on extension generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $V\in\mathcal C$, and $j^*$ restriction to its localized ringed site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be sheaves of commutative $O$-algebras with unital $O$-algebra transitions $q_{m,n}:B_m\to B_n$ for $m\ge n$, satisfying identity and composition. Put $B_{n,V}=j^*B_n$. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of module sheaves $M_n$ over $B_n$ with $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Define $\mathscr S(B_V)$ similarly, and let $J$ be termwise localized extension $j_{B_n!}$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For an $O_V$-module sheaf $G$ put $A_VG=(G\otimes_{O_V}B_{n,V})_n$, and for an $O$-module sheaf $H$ put $A_XH=(H\otimes_OB_n)_n$, with the strict maps $1\otimes q_{m,n}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The generator-normalized ordinary comparison of [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators], for $H=B_n$, has a canonical $B_n$-linear realization
$$a_{G,n}:(j_{O!}G)\otimes_OB_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{B_n!}(G\otimes_{O_V}B_{n,V}).$$
Here the underlying $O$-module identification between the two coefficient extensions is the unique identification preserving every extension-presheaf summand [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. These component maps give a natural isomorphism $a_G:A_Xj_{O!}G\xrightarrow{\sim}JA_VG$ in $\mathscr S(B)$, before scalar restriction. At every test object its component formula is $[x]_f\otimes b\mapsto[x\otimes b|_{(W,f)}]_f$. Every transition square is the equality
$$[x\otimes q_{m,n}(b)|_{(W,f)}]_f=[x\otimes q_{m,n}(b|_{(W,f)})]_f.$$
After forgetting to strict $O$-module towers, the square between extension and both scalar-unit augmentations commutes; its two composites on $[x]_f$ are $[x\otimes1]_f$. For a module map $v:G\to G'$, both naturality composites on $[x]_f\otimes b$ are $[v(x)\otimes b|_{(W,f)}]_f$. All these are equalities after bilinear sheafification, and the inverse component maps also commute with all transitions. Applying this natural isomorphism degreewise to any unbounded cochain complex gives a natural chain isomorphism of strict semilinear systems with the same transition, generator and augmentation identities [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. No flatness, surjectivity or completeness hypothesis on the coefficient system is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain AX and AV from scalar-tower construction and the extension functor from strict-system extension construction. Obtain the coefficient-linear component maps and forward compatibility squares from the level-comparison lemma.

Package the transported component maps as strict-system morphisms using their transition equations. Their naturality holds componentwise. Each component is invertible, being a composite of object equality maps, a component isomorphism and a functor image of an equality map. The componentwise invertibility criterion gives an isomorphism of strict systems, and NatIso.ofComponents packages its naturality. Apply the inverse component to its forward generator equation and cancel hom followed by inv to prove inverse_generator.

Retain the normalized scalar identification and uniqueness from the level comparison. To prove augmentation, use injectivity of the localized adjunction Hom correspondence to test the equality on original extension summands. The AX unit, the component generator formula, functoriality of extension on summands, the AV unit and the scalar-identification generator formula show both sides send [x] to [x tensor 1]. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to the constructed strict natural isomorphism. Its hom and inverse components in degree i are definitionally the original strict comparison and its inverse, so both chain degree equations are reflexivity. This is degreewise and imposes no boundedness condition.

(3) a = κ^{-1}∘ψ_{G,B_n}, using only the statement of lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators. (4) B_n-linearity is checked on generators via B_{n,V}(W,f)=B_n(W); the inverse is linear by injectivity. (5) both transition composites give [x⊗q(b)]_f, and the inverse square follows by cancellation. (6) naturality holds summandwise and in the first factor. (7) both augmentation composites give [x⊗1]_f by unitality, and sheafification uniqueness extends this. (8) the complex case is degreewise, so it holds unbounded.
